channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: BlackRock Raises EM Equities Back to Overweight on AI, Earnings
item.description: BlackRock Inc. has returned to an overweight recommendation on emerging-market equities, betting that access to the scarce resources needed for the artificial-intelligence boom and strong earnings will drive outperformance.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu

item.title: Markets Weigh AI Slowdown & Guardrails: Marc Franklin
item.description: Manulife Investment Management Head of Multi-Asset Solutions Marc Franklin argues that the recent AI stock pullback reflects debates surrounding regulatory guardrails and development pace rather than structural growth damage. He stresses that shifting regulatory frameworks and open-source quantum tools will create new competitive pressure for high-margin technology suppliers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Opposes AI Guardrails Amid Chip Selloff
item.description: Bloomberg's Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts break down how President Donald Trump's rejection of artificial intelligence safety guardrails coincides with a sharp selloff across semiconductor stocks. They also examine the regulatory uncertainty driving market movement and tech sector volatility. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ANZ CEO Warns of AI Risks and Job Cuts After Musk, Altman Alert
item.description: ANZ Group Holdings Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Nuno Matos warned about unpredictable risks linked to artificial intelligence and declined to rule out large-scale job cuts at the bank as it adopts the quickly evolving technology.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: Trump’s AI Defense Defies Voter Unease Heading Into Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump’s opposition to guardrails on artificial intelligence puts him at odds with a growing number of lawmakers from both parties, with AI safety fears adding to voters’ misgivings about the technology heading into the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Michael Shepard, Erik Wasson and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: AI Labs Should Make Safe Tech Without Antitrust Help, David Sacks Says
item.description: Top artificial intelligence companies Anthropic PBC and OpenAI should make safe products — and pace their own progress if necessary — without government intervention, David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science & Technology, said Monday in an interview with Bloomberg TV.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland and Ed Ludlow

item.title: DOJ Says Millions in Iran Oil Proceeds Laundered on Binance
item.description: The US Justice Department is seeking forfeiture of $61 million it says was generated from Iranian black-market oil sales and laundered through the cryptocurrency exchange Binance.
item.dc:creator: Ava Benny-Morrison

item.title: Authentic Brands’ Matt Maddox: Ready to IPO Early 2027
item.description: Matt Maddox, CEO of Authentic Brands, discusses why the company is partnering with creator Stephen Bartlett in a joint venture rather than pursuing a buyout-style deal. Maddox says Authentic Brands sees the creator economy as a major growth engine for media and audience expansion over the next decade, and views Bartlett as a strong partner for building brands through creator-led platforms. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gebru: AI Security & Safety Is About Human Control
item.description: Timnit Gebru DAIR Institute Founder & Executive Director, discusses her early warnings about artificial intelligence risks and her departure from Google’s ethical AI team in 2020. She discusses whether the public and policymakers are asking the right questions about AI safety and security, in the context of broader concerns about the pace of AI model development in the U.S. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chip Stocks Tumble on AI Safety Fears & Rising Yields
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Investment Management Deputy CIO, Solutions & Multi-Asset Jitania Kandhari, McKinsey & Co. Senior Partner & Global Leader, Tech & AI Kate Smaje, Teva Pharmaceuticals President & CEO Richard Francis, BetMGM CEO Adam Greenblatt, Texas Capital Bancshares CEO, Chairman, & President Rob Holmes, BlackRock US Head of Equity ETFs Jay Jacobs, The Distributed AI Research Institute Founder & Executive Director Timnit Gebru, Cloudfare CEO & Co-Founder Matthew Prince, Institute for Advanced Study, Harold F. Linder Professor Alondra Nelson, Thornburg Head of Fixed Income Christian Hoffmann, Starmoire CEO & Co-Founder Katie Palencsar & Starmoire Stylist Stacy London, & Authentic Brands CEO Matt Maddox. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Capital CEO on Moving to the Texas Stock Exchange
item.description: Texas Capital is switching its primary stock listing to the Texas Stock Exchange, joining Energy Transfer and other companies that plan to move starting in early October. In the segment, Rob Holmes, CEO of Texas Capital, is asked why the firm chose a full move to the TXSE rather than maintaining a dual listing with Nasdaq. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McKinsey AI Leader on the State of AI Development
item.description: Kate Smaje of McKinsey says the recent wave of warnings from AI leaders and researchers about slowing development is an important debate, especially around AGI, risk, pace, and patience. But she says the conversation inside boardrooms is different: executives who have already invested heavily in AI are now focused on whether those tools can scale, deliver profitability, and remain sustainable. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cloudflare CEO: Good Guys Have More Tools Than Bad Guys
item.description: Cloudflare CEO and Co-Founder Matthew Prince sits down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss AI's potential vulnerability, what's behind the bot traffic increase and if he agrees with Anthropic's Dario Amodei's warning. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Starmoire Launches With Stacy London as Chief Stylist
item.description: Katie Palencsar and Stacy London join Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick on The Close to discuss the launch of their end-to-end wardrobe management company, Starmoire. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Minebea Mitsumi Pauses M&A to Chase AI, Nvidia Demand for Components
item.description: Minebea Mitsumi Inc., one of Japan’s biggest corporate dealmakers, is hitting pause on acquisitions to focus on its output of ball bearings, motors and actuators for AI hardware to chase lucrative returns from the emerging technology.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Mochizuki

item.title: Carney Calls for Global Tech Body to Boost AI Guardrails
item.description: Canada wants to see the creation of a global “technology stability” body to help oversee AI and ensure it is safe, Prime Minister Mark Carney said in an interview with Bloomberg's Brian Platt (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Upcoming Apple Products: What to Expect in Late 2026 and Early 2027
item.description: Apple Inc. just launched some major new products, including the iPhone Duo, the iPhone 18 Pro line, AirPods 5 earbuds and fresh smartwatches. But the company has a lot more in store for this year and the first half of 2027.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: BCE to Expand Data Center Capacity in Saskatchewan
item.description: BCE Inc. plans to expand its data center campus in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan to as much as 1.2 gigawatts of capacity, the company announced Monday.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Hughes

item.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
item.description: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent days, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
item.dc:creator: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer

item.title: Accenture Settles With Justice Department Over DEI Policies
item.description: Accenture Plc, a management and technology consulting company, has agreed to pay $25 million to resolve allegations by the US Justice Department that it took race and sex into consideration when making hiring and promotion decisions.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins
